questions.question: Which of the following countries ranked 1st in the Global Innovation Index 2025 published by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Switzerland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Switzerland** has secured the **1st rank** in the **Global Innovation Index (GII) 2025**, continuing its long-standing dominance as the world's most innovative economy.
 
• The index is published annually by the **World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)**, a specialized agency of the **United Nations**.
 
• This ranking marks the **15th consecutive year** that **Switzerland** has been named the global leader in innovation, showcasing its robust **Research and Development (R&D)** ecosystem and high-quality **academic institutions**.
 
• Following **Switzerland**, other top-performing nations in the **2025 index** include **Sweden**, the **United States of America**, and **Singapore**, which consistently lead in technological advancements and patent filings.
 
• The **GII 2025** report highlights the state of global innovation trends, focusing on how **geopolitical tensions** and **economic shifts** influence the ability of nations to foster new ideas and industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of the Global Innovation Index (GII):**
 
 
• The **GII** relies on two sub-indices: the **Innovation Input Sub-Index** and the **Innovation Output Sub-Index**.
 
• The **Input Sub-Index** is built on five pillars: **Institutions**, **Human capital and research**, **Infrastructure**, **Market sophistication**, and **Business sophistication**.
 
• The **Output Sub-Index** is based on two pillars: **Knowledge and technology outputs** and **Creative outputs**.
 
• The overall score is the average of these two sub-indices, providing a balanced view of a country's innovation **enablers** and **results**.
 
 
 
• **World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO):**
 
 
• Established in **1967** and headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**, **WIPO** is the global forum for **intellectual property (IP)** services, policy, and cooperation.
 
• It currently has **193 member states** and manages over **26 international treaties** related to patents, trademarks, and industrial designs.
 
 
 
• **India's Performance:**
 
 
• India has shown significant growth in the **GII** over the last decade, consistently ranking as the **top innovative economy** in the **Central and Southern Asia** region.
 
• In recent editions like **2024**, India was ranked **39th** globally, driven by its leadership in **Information and Communication Technology (ICT)** services exports and **venture capital** receipt.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Top 5 Global Innovators (2025):** The top five positions are generally occupied by **Switzerland**, **Sweden**, the **United States**, **Singapore**, and the **United Kingdom**.
 
• **Science and Technology (S&T) Clusters:** The **GII** also ranks the world's top 100 **Science and Technology clusters**, with the **Tokyo-Yokohama** cluster in **Japan** and the **Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou** cluster in **China** often leading the list.
 
• **Impact of AI:** The **2025** report emphasizes the role of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Green Technologies** as the primary drivers of innovation growth for the current decade.
 
• **Global Innovation Tracker:** This component of the **GII** monitors key metrics like **scientific publications**, **venture capital deals**, and **international patent applications** (via the **Patent Cooperation Treaty - PCT**).
</ul

questions.question: In June 2025, how many enforcement actions did the Reserve Bank of India take across financial institutions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**353**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, as the primary regulatory authority for the financial sector, undertook a total of **353** enforcement actions during the month of **June 2025** to ensure strict adherence to banking norms.
 
• These **353** actions were distributed across various categories of financial entities, including **Public Sector Banks (PSBs)**, **Private Sector Banks**, **Foreign Banks**, and **Cooperative Banks**.
 
• The enforcement measures were primarily triggered by non-compliance with **regulatory guidelines**, specifically concerning **Know Your Customer (KYC)** requirements, **Anti-Money Laundering (AML)** standards, and the **Fair Practices Code**.
 
• The **Enforcement Department** of the **RBI**, which was centralized in **2017** to handle the imposition of penalties, oversaw the identification of these lapses and the subsequent execution of the **353** actions. ***Hence, the statement regarding the count of 353 actions is correct.***
 
• The nature of these actions varied from **monetary penalties** to **administrative censures** and **operational restrictions**, aimed at safeguarding the integrity of the Indian financial ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The **RBI** was established on **April 1, 1935**, in accordance with the provisions of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**. It serves as India's **Central Bank** and is responsible for **Monetary Policy** and the supervision of **banking and non-banking financial companies**.
 
• The **Governor** of the **RBI** leads the institution, which is headquartered in **Mumbai**, Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework for Enforcement:**
 
 
• The **RBI** derives its power to take enforcement actions and impose penalties from the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, particularly under **Section 47A**, and the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**.
 
• For **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)**, the **RBI** exercises authority under the **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Financial Entities Regulated:**
 
 
• **Public Sector Banks:** These are banks where the **Government of India** holds a majority stake (more than **50%**). There are currently **12** such banks in India.
 
• **Cooperative Banks:** These institutions are governed by both the **Banking Regulations Act** and **Cooperative Societies Acts** of the respective states. They play a vital role in **financial inclusion** in rural and semi-urban areas.
 
• **NBFCs:** These are entities registered under the **Companies Act** that provide banking services without meeting the legal definition of a bank.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of Enforcement Actions:**
 
 
• The primary objective is to maintain **Financial Stability** and protect the interests of **depositors**. By penalizing **353** entities in a single month, the **RBI** signals its zero-tolerance policy toward systemic risks and **fraudulent activities**.
 
• These actions also ensure that the **credit discipline** is maintained and that institutions do not engage in **evergreening of loans** or misreporting of **Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Enforcement Process:** The process begins with an **Annual Financial Inspection (AFI)**. If deficiencies are found, a **Show Cause Notice (SCN)** is issued. The final decision on the penalty, such as the **353** instances in **June 2025**, is taken after considering the institution's response.
 
• **Digital Lending Guidelines:** In recent years, a significant number of enforcement actions have been directed toward **Digital Lending Apps (DLAs)** and their **Lending Service Providers (LSPs)** for violating **consumer privacy** and **unethical recovery practices**.
 
• **Monetary Penalties:** The **quantum of penalty** is determined based on the **size of the entity** and the **severity of the violation**, ensuring the punishment is proportionate to the lapse.

questions.question: Which of the following missiles was successfully fired by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) on 24 September 2025 from a rail-mounted mobile launcher in coordination with the Strategic Forces Command?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Intermediate Range Agni-Prime Missile**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully flight-tested the **Intermediate Range Agni-Prime Missile** (also known as Agni-P) on **24 September 2025**.
 
• The test was conducted from a **rail-mounted mobile launcher**, demonstrating the capability for rapid deployment and high mobility across the Indian railway network.
 
• This successful mission was carried out in close coordination with the **Strategic Forces Command (SFC)**, which is responsible for the management and administration of the country's tactical and strategic nuclear weapons stockpile.
 
• The **Agni-Prime** is a **two-stage canisterised solid-propellant** ballistic missile. Being canisterised allows for the missile to be stored for long periods and launched with very short preparation time.
 
• The missile has a strike range capability between **1,000 and 2,000 kilometres**, making it a critical asset for regional deterrence.
 
• The test validated the reliability and efficiency of the advanced propulsion systems, navigation, and control mechanisms integrated into the **Agni-P** platform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Agni Series Evolution:**
 
 
• The **Agni-P** is a next-generation follow-on to the **Agni-I** and **Agni-II** missiles, incorporating technologies used in the longer-range **Agni-IV** and **Agni-V**.
 
• **Agni-I**: Range of **700-800 km**.
 
• **Agni-V**: India's first Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) with a range exceeding **5,000 km**.
 
 
 
• **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):**
 
 
• It was established in **1958** by merging the Technical Development Establishment of the Indian Army and the Directorate of Technical Development and Production.
 
• It works under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India, with headquarters in **New Delhi**.
 
• Its primary objective is to achieve self-reliance in critical defence technologies and systems.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Forces Command (SFC):**
 
 
• Created in **January 2003**, the SFC is a part of India's **Nuclear Command Authority (NCA)**.
 
• It is responsible for operationalising the directives of the NCA under the leadership of a Commander-in-Chief of the rank of Air Marshal or equivalent.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advanced Navigation:** The **Agni-Prime** missile features a **Ring Laser Gyro-based Inertial Navigation System (RINS)** and a redundant **Micro Navigation System (MINS)** to ensure high-degree accuracy during terminal phases.
 
• **Weight and Maneuverability:** Compared to earlier versions, the **Agni-P** is significantly lighter due to the use of composite materials, making it easier to transport via **road or rail**.
 
• **Strategic Significance:** The development of the **Intermediate Range Agni-Prime** strengthens India's **No First Use (NFU)** nuclear doctrine by ensuring a credible and survivable second-strike capability.
 
• **BrahMos (Option 1):** This is a **Supersonic Cruise Missile** developed jointly by **India (DRDO)** and **Russia (NPOM)**, with a range of approximately **290-450 km**, fundamentally different from the ballistic Agni series.
 
• **Akash (Option 3):** This is a short-range **Surface-to-Air Missile (SAM)** system designed to protect vulnerable areas from air attacks.
 
• **Prithvi-II (Option 4):** A short-range surface-to-surface **ballistic missile** with a range of approximately **250-350 km**, first tested in **1996**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following lunar missions became the first to detect over 250 seismic signals from the Moon’s south pole, marking a significant advancement in lunar exploration since the Apollo missions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandrayaan-3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandrayaan-3** is the third lunar exploration mission by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, which successfully landed near the **Moon’s south pole** on **August 23, 2023**.
 
• The mission's **Vikram lander** was equipped with the **Instrument for Lunar Seismic Activity (ILSA)**, which became the first instrument to detect over **250 seismic signals** from the polar region.
 
• The **ILSA** payload is designed to characterize the **seismicity** of the lunar surface by measuring ground vibrations caused by **moonquakes**, **meteorite impacts**, and artificial activities like the movement of the **Pragyan rover**.
 
• This marks a significant scientific leap because seismic data from the Moon had not been collected since the **Apollo missions** of the **1970s**, which were primarily located around the **lunar equator**.
 
• By detecting these signals at the **south pole**, **Chandrayaan-3** has provided researchers with a new dataset to understand the **lunar crust** and **mantle** structure in a previously unexplored geographical context.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ILSA Technology**: The instrument is built using **Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS)** technology. This allowed the seismometer to be compact and highly sensitive, capable of detecting vibrations as small as a few **nanometers**.
 
• **The Pragyan Rover**: During its mission life of **14 Earth days** (one lunar day), the **Pragyan rover** traveled over **100 meters**. Interestingly, the **ILSA** was sensitive enough to record the vibrations generated by the **rover's wheels** as it navigated the lunar terrain.
 
• **Mission Components**: **Chandrayaan-3** consisted of a **Lander Module (Vikram)**, a **Rover (Pragyan)**, and a **Propulsion Module**. The **Propulsion Module** carried the **SHAPE** (Spectro-polarimetry of Habitable Planet Earth) payload to study Earth from lunar orbit.
 
• **Other Missions**:
 
 
• **Chang'e 5**: A **Chinese** mission launched in **2020** that successfully returned **lunar soil samples** to Earth but did not focus on long-term seismic monitoring at the south pole.
 
• **Luna 1**: The first spacecraft to reach the vicinity of the Moon, launched by the **Soviet Union** in **1959**.
 
• **Artemis I**: An uncrewed **NASA** mission launched in **2022** as a flight test for the **Orion** spacecraft and the **Space Launch System (SLS)**, orbiting the Moon without landing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shiv Shakti Point**: The landing site of **Chandrayaan-3** was officially named **Shiv Shakti Point** by the **Government of India** to commemorate the success of the mission.
 
• **LVM3-M4**: The heavy-lift launch vehicle, also known as the **Launch Vehicle Mark-III**, was used to propel the spacecraft into space from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota**.
 
• **Global Achievement**: With this mission, **India** became the **fourth country** to achieve a soft landing on the Moon and the **first** to do so in the **lunar south pole region**.
 
• **Scientific Payloads**: Apart from **ILSA**, the mission included **ChaSTE** to measure thermal properties and **APXS** and **LIBS** on the rover to determine the **elemental composition** of lunar soil, which confirmed the presence of **Sulphur**.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) satellite launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota in July 2025?

options.text: To strengthen military surveillance and border security operations
To enhance global monitoring of climate change and natural disasters
To improve global internet connectivity through satellite communication
To explore deep space and study distant planetary atmospheres

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To enhance global monitoring of climate change and natural disasters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **NASA–ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR)** is a joint Earth-observing mission between the **National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)** and the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• The primary objective of this mission is to track subtle changes in the **Earth's surface**, providing essential data for understanding **climate change**, **deforestation**, **glacier melt**, and **natural hazards** such as **earthquakes**, **tsunamis**, **volcanoes**, and **landslides**. ***Hence, the correct answer is To enhance global monitoring of climate change and natural disasters.***
 
• The satellite is scheduled to be launched from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota**, India, using the **GSLV Mark II** (or LVM3) launch vehicle in **July 2025**.
 
• **NISAR** will be the first satellite mission to use two different radar frequencies, the **L-band** and the **S-band**, to measure changes in our planet's surface less than a centimeter across.
 
• The mission is designed to observe the entire land and ice masses of the **Earth** every **12 days**, providing a consistent and detailed time-lapse view of planetary changes over its **three-year** primary mission life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Technological Contribution:** 
 
 
• **NASA** is providing the **L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar**, a high-rate communication subsystem for science data, **GPS** receivers, a solid-state recorder, and the payload data subsystem.
 
• **ISRO** is providing the **S-band radar**, the spacecraft bus, the **GSLV** launch system, and associated launch services.
 
 
 
• **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR):** Unlike optical sensors, **SAR** can penetrate **clouds**, **smoke**, and **forest canopies**, and can operate during both day and night, making it an invaluable tool for **disaster management** and **environmental monitoring**.
 
• **Global Ecosystems:** The mission will measure changes in **vegetation biomass**, which is crucial for understanding the **carbon cycle** and the impact of **human activities** on **forests** and **wetlands**.
 
• **Cryosphere Monitoring:** **NISAR** will monitor the flow rates of **glaciers** and **ice sheets** in **Antarctica** and **Greenland**, helping scientists predict future **sea-level rise** more accurately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Data Accessibility:** One of the most significant aspects of the **NISAR** mission is that the data collected will be **free and open** to the public, facilitating global research and **scientific collaboration**.
 
• **Disaster Response:** In the event of large-scale **natural disasters**, **NISAR** data will be used to assess the extent of damage and help in **relief operations** by providing high-resolution maps of the affected regions.
 
• **Solid Earth:** The mission will study **crustal deformation**, providing insights into the processes occurring deep within the **Earth** that lead to **tectonic shifts** and **volcanic eruptions**.
 
• **Indo-US Cooperation:** This project represents one of the largest and most complex **space collaborations** between **India** and the **United States**, strengthening bilateral ties in **science and technology**.

questions.question: In June 2025, Standard & Poor's (S&P) Global Ratings revised India’s gross domestic product (GDP) growth forecast for FY26 to _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.5%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the global credit rating agency **S&P Global Ratings** (Standard & Poor's) updated its economic outlook for **India**, specifically revising the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** growth forecast for the fiscal year **2025-26 (FY26)**.
 
• The agency settled on a growth projection of **6.5%** for **FY26**, indicating a steady but moderated growth trajectory compared to previous high-growth years.
 
• The revision by **S&P** typically takes into account various macroeconomic indicators such as **inflation trends**, **interest rate** trajectories set by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, and the overall **global economic environment**.
 
• Growth in **FY26** is expected to be supported by a gradual recovery in **rural demand** and continued **government capital expenditure** on infrastructure projects, which acts as a catalyst for private investment.
 
• The forecast of **6.5%** reflects the agency's view on the balance between **domestic consumption** and external challenges, such as volatile **commodity prices** and shifts in global **supply chains**.
 
• **S&P Global Ratings** often aligns its forecasts with the expected performance of the **services sector** and the **manufacturing sector**, which remain the primary drivers of the **Indian economy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **S&P Global Ratings:**
 
 
• It is one of the **"Big Three"** credit rating agencies globally, alongside **Moody’s Investors Service** and **Fitch Ratings**. 
 
• Headquartered in the **United States**, it provides essential intelligence, including **credit ratings**, **benchmarks**, and **economic research** to investors and market participants worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP):**
 
 
• **GDP** measures the total market value of all final **goods and services** produced within a country's geographical boundaries during a specific **financial year**.
 
• It is the most common indicator used to track the health and size of a **national economy**.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Year (FY) in India:**
 
 
• In **India**, the **Fiscal Year** runs from **April 1st** to **March 31st**. 
 
• The term **FY26** refers to the period starting from **April 1, 2025**, and ending on **March 31, 2026**.
 
 
 
• **Other Forecasting Entities:**
 
 
• Besides **S&P**, other institutions like the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**, the **World Bank**, and the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** regularly release **GDP growth** estimates.
 
• These projections are crucial for **policymakers** to formulate the **Union Budget** and for **foreign investors** to make decisions regarding **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing GDP Growth:**
 
 
• Key components influencing these percentages include **Private Final Consumption Expenditure (PFCE)**, **Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF)**, and the **Net Export** status of the country.
 
• A growth rate of **6.5%** generally positions **India** as one of the fastest-growing major economies in the world.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Economic revisions are dynamic; for instance, if **monetary easing** (lowering of **repo rates**) occurs faster than expected in **2025**, the growth might exceed the **6.5%** mark.
 
• **Inflation management** remains a core focus for the **RBI**, as maintaining **CPI inflation** within the target band of **4% (+/- 2%)** is essential for sustainable **GDP growth**.
 
• The **June 2025** report by **S&P** serves as a mid-year benchmark for tracking the **Indian economy's** resilience against global headwinds like **geopolitical tensions**.

questions.question: What is the title of the 2025 UNICEF report on child nutrition?

options.text: Nourish the Next: Global Nutrition Review
Feeding Profit: How Food Environments Are Failing Children
Growing Well: Global Child Nutrition Index

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Feeding Profit: How Food Environments Are Failing Children**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **2025** flagship report released by **UNICEF** is titled **Feeding Profit: How Food Environments Are Failing Children**, which focuses on the systemic failures of the **global food system**.
 
• The report highlights a critical shift where **commercial interests** and the drive for **profit** often outweigh the **nutritional well-being** and health of **infants**, **children**, and **adolescents**.
 
• It reveals that nearly **one in three** children globally are not growing well due to **malnutrition**, which is increasingly driven by the high availability of **ultra-processed foods** and **sugary drinks**.
 
• The **UNICEF** findings underscore that **poor food environments**—characterized by **aggressive marketing** and **low affordability** of fresh produce—are the primary drivers of the **childhood obesity** epidemic.
 
• The report calls for **national governments** to implement **stricter regulations** on the **food industry** to protect children from **unhealthy food exposures** and ensure access to **diverse** and **nutritious diets**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund):**

 
 
• Established in **1946** and headquartered in **New York City**, **UNICEF** is a **United Nations** agency responsible for providing **humanitarian** and **developmental aid** to children worldwide.
 
• Its **nutrition programs** aim to prevent **stunting**, **wasting**, and **micronutrient deficiencies** in more than **190 countries**.
 
 
 
• **Malnutrition Trends:**
 
 
• The **Triple Burden of Malnutrition** refers to the coexistence of **undernutrition** (stunting and wasting), **micronutrient deficiencies**, and **overweight/obesity** within the same community or household.
 
• Data from **2023-2024** indicates that approximately **148 million** children under **5 years** of age suffer from **stunting** globally.
 
 
 
• **Food Environments:**
 
 
• This term refers to the **physical**, **economic**, and **policy conditions** that shape food **accessibility**, **affordability**, and **promotional messaging**.
 
• **Healthy food environments** are essential for achieving **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 2**, which targets **Zero Hunger** and improved **nutrition** by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Ultra-Processed Foods (UPFs):**
 
 
• These are **industrial formulations** typically high in **sodium**, **free sugars**, and **saturated fats**, but low in **protein** and **fiber**.
 
• The **2025 report** identifies **UPFs** as a major contributor to **non-communicable diseases (NCDs)** such as **Type 2 diabetes** and **hypertension** starting in early **childhood**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Measures:**

 
 
• To combat **malnutrition**, experts suggest **front-of-package labeling**, **taxes on sugar-sweetened beverages**, and **bans on marketing** unhealthy foods to **minor children**.
 
• Several **Latin American countries**, such as **Chile** and **Mexico**, have already pioneered **black-label warning systems** to inform consumers about high levels of **sugar** and **fat**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The **World Bank** estimates that **malnutrition** can cost the **global economy** billions of dollars in **lost productivity** and **healthcare expenses**.
 
• Investing in **child nutrition** yields high returns, often estimated at **$16** for every **$1** spent on **interventions**.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers was affected by flash floods triggered by torrential rain in Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kheer Ganga River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **August 2025**, the **Kheer Ganga River** was severely affected by flash floods following intense **torrential rain** and suspected **cloudbursts** in its upper catchment areas.
 
• The disaster occurred in the **Uttarkashi district** of **Uttarakhand**, a region highly susceptible to extreme weather events during the **monsoon season**.
 
• The sudden increase in the water level of the **Kheer Ganga**, which is a tributary of the **Bhagirathi River**, led to the destruction of local bridges and temporary settlements.
 
• Rescue operations were promptly initiated by the **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)** to assist residents and pilgrims stranded in the affected zones near **Ghattu Gad** and surrounding valleys.
 
• The surge in the **Kheer Ganga** also caused a temporary rise in the silt levels and water volume of the main **Bhagirathi River**, prompting alerts in downstream towns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Context of Uttarkashi:**
 
 
• **Uttarkashi** is a border district in **Uttarakhand**, housing the origins of two of India's holiest rivers: the **Ganga (as Bhagirathi)** and the **Yamuna**.
 
• The district is part of the **Garhwal Himalayas** and is characterized by steep slopes and narrow valleys, making it prone to **landslides** and **flash floods**.
 
 
 
• **Bhagirathi River:**
 
 
• The **Bhagirathi** is considered the source stream of the **Ganga**, originating from the **Gaumukh** at the foot of the **Gangotri Glacier**.
 
• It flows for about **205 kilometers** before meeting the **Alaknanda River** at **Devprayag**.
 
 
 
• **Mandakini River:**
 
 
• The **Mandakini** originates from the **Chorabari Glacier** near **Kedarnath** in the **Rudraprayag district**.
 
• It was the primary river involved in the catastrophic **2013 North India floods**, but it is not the river affected in this specific **2025 Uttarkashi** event.
 
 
 
• **Alaknanda River:**
 
 
• The **Alaknanda** rises in the **Satopanth Glacier** and **Bhagirath Kharak Glacier** in **Chamoli district**.
 
• It is one of the major tributaries of the **Ganga** and has several confluences known as the **Panch Prayag**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Meteorological Factors:** The **August 2025** floods were triggered by a **low-pressure system** that caused localized heavy downpours, often exceeding **100 mm** of rain within a few hours.
 
• **Ecological Sensitivity:** The **Himalayan region** is an **Eco-Sensitive Zone** where unplanned construction and **climate change** have increased the frequency of **GLOFs (Glacial Lake Outburst Floods)** and flash floods.
 
• **Disaster Management:** The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** and the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** emphasize the use of **Early Warning Systems (EWS)** to mitigate such risks in the **high-altitude** districts of **Uttarakhand**.
</ul

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chief Minister of Delhi following the 2025 elections?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rekha Gupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rekha Gupta** was appointed as the **Chief Minister** of **Delhi** following the results of the **2025 Delhi Legislative Assembly elections**.
 
• She represents the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, which emerged as the majority party by securing a significant number of seats in the **70-member assembly**.
 
• The appointment was formalized after the **Lieutenant Governor** of **Delhi** invited the leader of the single largest party to form the government, leading to her swearing-in ceremony in **February 2025**.
 
• As the **Chief Minister**, she heads the **Council of Ministers** of the **National Capital Territory (NCT)** of **Delhi**, overseeing administrative and executive functions within the state’s jurisdiction.
 
• Her victory marked a major political transition in the capital, shifting the governance from the **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)** to the **BJP** after a decade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Delhi Legislative Assembly**:
 
 
• The **Legislative Assembly** of **Delhi** consists of **70 members** elected directly by the people.
 
• The **term** of the assembly is **five years**, as mandated by the **Constitution of India**, unless it is dissolved earlier.
 
• The majority mark required to form a government in the **70-member house** is **36 seats**.
 
 
 
• **Article 239AA**:
 
 
• This article of the **Indian Constitution** provides **special status** to **Delhi** as the **National Capital Territory**.
 
• It stipulates that there shall be a **Legislative Assembly** and a **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Chief Minister** to aid and advise the **Lieutenant Governor**.
 
• The **Parliament** of India retains control over specific subjects like **Public Order**, **Police**, and **Land** in **Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Lieutenant Governor (LG)**:
 
 
• The **LG** is the **Constitutional Head** of the **NCT of Delhi** and is appointed by the **President of India**.
 
• In the **2025** political context, the **LG** administered the **Oath of Office and Secrecy** to the new **Chief Minister** and the cabinet members at **Raj Niwas**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atishi Marlena**: Prior to the **2025 elections**, she served as the **Chief Minister** of **Delhi**, having taken office in **September 2024** following the resignation of **Arvind Kejriwal**.
 
• **Arvind Kejriwal**: He served as the **Chief Minister** for three consecutive terms (**2013**, **2015-2020**, and **2020-2024**) before stepping down in **2024**; he led the **AAP** campaign during the **2025** polls.
 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**: The **ECI** was responsible for conducting the **2025 Delhi Assembly elections**, ensuring a free and fair voting process for millions of registered voters in the capital.
 
• **Governance Structure**: Unlike other **Union Territories**, **Delhi** has a unique dual-governance model where the elected government and the **Central Government** (through the **LG**) share administrative responsibilities.

questions.question: Which of the following two main types of support are provided to rural families under the Poverty‑Free Village Scheme launched by Rajasthan in July 2025?

options.text: Health insurance coverage and credit loans

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cash assistance and employment opportunities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Poverty-Free Village Scheme** was launched by the **Government of Rajasthan** in **July 2025** to uplift the socio-economic status of rural inhabitants.
 
• The scheme specifically focuses on providing **Cash assistance** to help families meet their immediate financial needs and manage daily subsistence costs.
 
• Along with financial aid, the initiative emphasizes **Employment opportunities** by integrating rural workers into local developmental projects and infrastructure maintenance. ***Hence, the correct answer is Cash assistance and employment opportunities.***
 
• The primary objective of this project is to ensure that no household in the selected **Gram Panchayats** falls below the **Poverty Line** by the end of the implementation cycle.
 
• Implementation is carried out through the **Department of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj**, ensuring that the benefits reach the grassroots level effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Target Groups:** The scheme is designed for **rural families** who are identified through the **SECC (Socio-Economic and Caste Census)** data and those currently lacking stable income sources.
 
• **Mechanism of Cash Assistance:** The funds are disbursed through **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries, ensuring transparency and reducing leakage. The estimated monthly support varies based on **family size** and **economic distress levels**.
 
• **Employment Generation:** 
 
 
• The **Employment opportunities** component includes a **150-day guaranteed work** clause, which is an extension beyond the standard provisions of **MGNREGA**.
 
• It also includes **Skill Development training** programs to make the youth in these villages employable in nearby **Industrial Clusters**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Coverage:** While the pilot phase started in specific districts like **Jaipur** and **Jodhpur**, the state aims to cover over **10,000 villages** across **Rajasthan** by the year **2027**.
 
• **Monitoring and Evaluation:** A specialized **Digital Dashboard** has been created to track the poverty status of every enrolled family in real-time, involving **Social Audits** conducted by local community groups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility Criteria:** Families must be residents of **Rajasthan** for at least **10 years** and should not have a member employed in a **Government Job** or paying **Income Tax**.
 
• **Sustainable Goals:** This scheme aligns with the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 1 (No Poverty)** and **Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth)**.
 
• **Integration:** It works in tandem with other state welfare programs such as the **Chiranjeevi Health Insurance Scheme** to provide a holistic safety net, although health insurance is not the core component of this specific "Poverty-Free" grant.
</ul

questions.question: In which city was the 23rd edition of the National Para Athletics Championships, 2025, organised?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chennai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **23rd edition** of the **National Para Athletics Championships, 2025**, was organized in the city of **Chennai**, **Tamil Nadu**.
 
• The championship was held from **January 9 to January 13, 2025**, at the iconic **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium**.
 
• The event was organized by the **Paralympic Committee of India (PCI)** in collaboration with the **Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT)** and the **Tamil Nadu Para Sports Association**.
 
• The 2025 edition saw the participation of approximately **2,500 athletes** representing **28 states** and **8 Union Territories** across various sporting categories.
 
• This national meet serves as a crucial selection trial for identifying and grooming athletes for upcoming international competitions, including the **World Para Athletics Championships** and the **Asian Para Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Paralympic Committee of India (PCI):**
 
 
• The **PCI** was founded in **1992** and is the national governing body for para-sports in the country.
 
• It is recognized by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of India, and is affiliated with the **International Paralympic Committee (IPC)**.
 
• The current President of the **PCI** is **Devendra Jhajharia**, who is a two-time **Paralympic gold medalist** in javelin throw.
 
 
 
• **Classification in Para Athletics:**
 
 
• Athletes are grouped into **classes** based on their physical, visual, or intellectual impairments to ensure fair competition.
 
• Prefix **"T"** stands for **Track** and **Jumping** events, while **"F"** stands for **Field** events (like shot put or discus).
 
• The numeric values indicate the type and severity of the impairment; for example, **classes 11-13** are for visually impaired athletes, while **classes 51-57** are for athletes competing in wheelchairs.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu as a Sports Hub:**
 
 
• The state of **Tamil Nadu** has been proactive in promoting sports through the **SDAT**, having recently hosted the **Khelo India Youth Games** in **2024**.
 
• The **Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium** in **Chennai**, built in **1993**, has a seating capacity of **40,000** and is a premier venue for national and international athletic meets.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the National Championships:**
 
 
• The **National Para Athletics Championship** is the highest level of domestic competition for para-athletes in India.
 
• Performance in this event is the primary criterion for the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, which provides financial and technical assistance to top athletes.
 
• The **23rd edition** featured a wide range of events including **100m, 200m, 400m, 1500m sprints**, **Long Jump**, **High Jump**, **Shot Put**, **Discus Throw**, and **Club Throw**.
 
• India’s recent success at the **Paris 2024 Paralympics**, where the country won a record **29 medals**, has significantly boosted the profile and funding for these national meets.

questions.question: As per the Sustainable Development Goals — National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2025, published in June 2025, what percentage of the rural population used improved sources of drinking water during the year 2024–2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**99.62%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals — National Indicator Framework (NIF) Progress Report, 2025**, was released in **June 2025** by the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**.
 
• According to the report, during the assessment year **2024–2025**, the percentage of the **rural population** using improved sources of drinking water reached **99.62%**. ***Hence, the correct option is 99.62%.***
 
• This indicator is a vital metric under **SDG Goal 6**, which specifically targets **Clean Water and Sanitation** for all citizens.
 
• The data indicates a significant upward trajectory in rural infrastructure development, ensuring that nearly the entire rural landscape has access to safe and improved water sources.
 
• The report serves as a monitoring tool for the **United Nations' 2030 Agenda**, tracking India's specific progress through the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)**, which currently consists of over **300 indicators**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation):** 
 
 
• This goal aims to ensure the **availability and sustainable management of water** and sanitation for all by the year **2030**.
 
• India's commitment to this goal is reflected in large-scale schemes designed to eliminate the disparity between **urban** and **rural** access.
 
 
 
• **Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM):** 
 
 
• Launched on **15th August 2019**, this mission is a primary driver for the high percentage recorded in the 2025 report.
 
• The mission aims to provide **Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC)** to every rural household, often referred to as **"Har Ghar Jal,"** by **2024-25**.
 
• It emphasizes **community-based management** and greywater treatment to ensure long-term sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Improved Sources of Drinking Water:** 
 
 
• This category includes **piped water** into dwellings, **public taps** or standpipes, **tube wells** or boreholes, protected dug wells, and **rainwater harvesting** systems.
 
• The use of improved sources is critical in reducing **water-borne diseases** such as cholera, dysentery, and typhoid in **rural India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI):** 
 
 
• **MoSPI** is the nodal agency in India responsible for the development of the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)**.
 
• It coordinates with various **Central Ministries** and **State Governments** to collect authenticated data for the **SDG Progress Reports**.
 
 
 
• **National Indicator Framework (NIF):** 
 
 
• The **NIF** is the backbone of **SDG monitoring** in India, localized to suit the Indian context while remaining aligned with **Global Indicators**.
 
• The **2025 Progress Report** highlights that India has made "substantial progress" in **Goal 6**, with the rural drinking water target being one of the most successful outcomes.
 
• Data for this specific indicator is often sourced from the **Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
